records.source: Καί τινες κατελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐδίδασκον τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ περιτμηθῆτε τῷ ἔθει τῷ Μωϋσέως, οὐ δύνασθε σωθῆναι.
records.gloss: And certain ones having come down from Judea were teaching the brothers, If not you are circumcised by the custom of Moses, not you are able to be saved.
pieces: Some people came down from Judea and began teaching the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, "Unless you are circumcised as the custom of Moses requires, there is no way for you to be saved."

L.1: And some who had come down from Judea were teaching the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, "If you are not circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."

R.1: Some people came to Antioch from Judea. They began to teach the believers there, "God's law given through Moses says that men must be circumcised. If you are not circumcised, God will not save you."

decisions.choice: circumcised: the rite that marked a Jewish man as belonging to God's covenant people
alternatives: a matter of health or custom only
decisions.reason: God gave circumcision to Abraham as the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:9-14), and the law of Moses repeats it (Leviticus 12:3). A Gentile man who joined Israel was circumcised (Exodus 12:48). The teachers say that Gentile believers must do the same.

decisions.choice: the custom of Moses: the way of life laid down in the law given through Moses
alternatives: a human tradition added to the law
decisions.reason: Luke uses "customs" for the practices of the Jewish law (6:14, 21:21, 28:17). In 15:5 the same demand is put as keeping "the law of Moses".

decisions.choice: a condition for salvation: no circumcision, no salvation
alternatives: advice about the best way to live
decisions.reason: The sentence makes circumcision a requirement for being saved, not a matter of custom only. That is the question the council takes up (15:11).

decisions.choice: some: people not named, who came from Judea
alternatives: officially sent by the Jerusalem church
decisions.reason: The letter in 15:24 says the church in Jerusalem gave them no instructions. Luke tells where they came from, not who they were. The scene is Antioch, where Paul and Barnabas had returned (14:26-28).

decisions.choice: came to Antioch from Judea; men must be circumcised
alternatives: some who had come down from Judea
decisions.reason: Readable names the place, from 14:26-28, and says that circumcision applied to men. It also spells out the condition as two sentences.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow believers, men and women. Readable says so plainly, as Acts 1-6 does in places.

records.heading: The question of circumcision

records.source: γενομένης δὲ στάσεως καὶ ζητήσεως οὐκ ὀλίγης τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔταξαν ἀναβαίνειν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν καί τινας ἄλλους ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ τοῦ ζητήματος τούτου.
records.gloss: Having arisen then commotion and discussion not small by Paul and Barnabas with them, they appointed to go up Paul and Barnabas and certain others out from them to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about the question this.
pieces: This led to fierce dispute and argument between them and Paul and Barnabas. So it was arranged that Paul and Barnabas and some others from among them should go up to Jerusalem and put this question to the apostles and the elders.

L.2: And when there had been no small dissension and debate between Paul and Barnabas and them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others of them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem concerning this question.

R.2: Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed with these men, and they argued with them for a long time. So the believers chose Paul and Barnabas and some others to go to Jerusalem. They were to ask the apostles and the elders about this question.

decisions.choice: no small: a great deal of, fierce
decisions.reason: Saying "not small" to mean "great" is a habit of Luke's (12:18, 14:28, 19:23, 19:24).

decisions.choice: dissension: a sharp clash of views, a quarrel
decisions.reason: The word can mean a revolt (19:40, 24:5), but with "debate" beside it, it means a heated dispute (23:7, 23:10).

decisions.choice: they appointed: the believers at Antioch
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. The church at Antioch sends them on their way in 15:3, so the believers there are the ones who appointed them.

decisions.choice: the elders: leaders of the Jerusalem church, beside the apostles
alternatives: the elders of the Jewish council
decisions.reason: The church in Jerusalem had elders as early as 11:30. They are named with the apostles throughout this chapter (15:4, 15:6, 15:22, 15:23) and again in 16:4.

decisions.choice: go up: Jerusalem is high in the hills, and the city of the temple
decisions.reason: People spoke of going up to Jerusalem from any direction (11:2, 18:22, 21:12).

decisions.choice: the believers chose
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, following the meaning note.

records.source: οἱ μὲν οὖν προπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διήρχοντο τήν τε Φοινίκην καὶ Σαμάρειαν ἐκδιηγούμενοι τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἐποίουν χαρὰν μεγάλην πᾶσι τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
records.gloss: They indeed therefore having been sent forward by the church were passing through both Phoenicia and Samaria relating in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and they were bringing joy great to all the brothers.
pieces: The church sent them off, and as they went through Phoenicia and Samaria they told in full how the Gentiles were turning to God. The news brought great joy to all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

L.3: So they, having been sent on their way by the church, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, describing in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and they brought great joy to all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

R.3: The church at Antioch helped them start their trip. They went through Phoenicia and Samaria and told the believers there all about how Gentiles were turning to God. This news filled all the believers with joy.

decisions.choice: sent on their way: helped on the journey with supplies and company
decisions.reason: Sending travelers on their way meant providing for the journey and going part of the way with them (20:38, 21:5; Romans 15:24; Titus 3:13).

decisions.choice: conversion: turning from idols to God
decisions.reason: The noun is related to the verb for turning to God used in 14:15, 15:19 and 26:20 (1 Thessalonians 1:9).

decisions.choice: Phoenicia and Samaria: the coast road south from Syria, then the hill country north of Judea
decisions.reason: There were believers in both (8:5-25, 11:19). The journey took them through churches that had themselves begun outside Judea.

decisions.choice: the church at Antioch; told the believers there
decisions.reason: Readable names the church and says to whom they told the news, which the end of the sentence implies.

decisions.choice: were turning to God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what conversion means here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: all the believers
decisions.reason: As at 15:1.

records.source: παραγενόμενοι δὲ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρεδέχθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀνήγγειλάν τε ὅσα ὁ θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Having come then to Jerusalem they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders, they declared then all that the God had done with them.
pieces: On reaching Jerusalem they were received by the church, the apostles and the elders, and they told them everything God had done in company with them.

L.4: And when they arrived in Jerusalem, they were received by the church and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all that God had done with them.

R.4: When they got to Jerusalem, the church, the apostles and the elders welcomed them. Paul and Barnabas told them about all the things that God had done as they worked with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: with them: God working together with them, at their side
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 14:27. God is the one who acts, and they work with him; Paul says the same in 1 Corinthians 3:9. Some take it simply as "through them", which 15:12 says.

decisions.choice: received: welcomed as guests and fellow believers
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive kindly, as of welcoming a guest.

decisions.choice: in company with them
decisions.reason: Balanced makes clear that "with" means working beside them, not merely in their presence.

decisions.choice: Paul and Barnabas told them; as they worked with him
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers and spells out the sense of "with them", as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἐξανέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φαρισαίων πεπιστευκότες, λέγοντες ὅτι δεῖ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς παραγγέλλειν τε τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως.
records.gloss: Rose up now certain of those of the sect of the Pharisees who believed, saying that It is necessary to circumcise them, to command [them] then to keep the law of Moses.
pieces: Then some from the party of the Pharisees who had believed stood up and insisted, "These Gentiles have to be circumcised, and they must be ordered to keep the law of Moses."

L.5: But some of those of the party of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying, "It is necessary to circumcise them and to command [them] to keep the law of Moses."

R.5: But some of the believers had been Pharisees, and they still belonged to that group. They stood up and said, "The Gentile believers must be circumcised. And they must be told to obey all the law that God gave through Moses."

decisions.choice: the party of the Pharisees: a Jewish movement known for strict keeping of the law
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same word for the Sadducees (5:17), and Paul calls the Pharisees "the strictest party of our religion" (26:5). Paul himself was a Pharisee (23:6; Philippians 3:5).

decisions.choice: who had believed: these Pharisees were themselves believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: The perfect participle describes people who had come to faith and still held it. The dispute is inside the church.

decisions.choice: them: the Gentiles who had believed
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to the Gentiles whose conversion was reported in 15:3-4.

decisions.choice: it is necessary: a requirement, not advice
decisions.reason: The word means what must happen. It matches the demand in 15:1.

decisions.choice: these Gentiles; the Gentile believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whom "them" means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: some of the believers had been Pharisees, and they still belonged to that group
alternatives: some of the party of the Pharisees who had believed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that these were believers who belonged to the party of the Pharisees.

records.source: Συνήχθησάν τε οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἰδεῖν περὶ τοῦ λόγου τούτου.
records.gloss: Were gathered together then the apostles and the elders to see about the matter this.
pieces: The apostles and the elders came together to consider this matter.

L.6: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to look into this matter.

R.6: So the apostles and the elders met to talk about this question.

decisions.choice: to see about: to look into, to consider and decide
decisions.reason: "To see about" a matter means to examine it (18:15).

decisions.choice: the apostles and the elders: the leaders who meet to decide
alternatives: the leaders only, with no one else present
decisions.reason: The leaders are named here, but 15:12 speaks of "the whole crowd" falling silent, and 15:22 says the decision pleased "the whole church". The meeting seems to have taken place with the church present.

records.heading: The apostles and the elders consider the matter

records.source: πολλῆς δὲ ζητήσεως γενομένης ἀναστὰς Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἀφ’ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ στόματός μου ἀκοῦσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὸν λόγον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ πιστεῦσαι, καὶ ὁ καρδιογνώστης θεὸς ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτοῖς δοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καθὼς καὶ ἡμῖν, καὶ οὐθὲν διέκρινεν μεταξὺ ἡμῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν, τῇ πίστει καθαρίσας τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Of much now discussion having taken place, having risen up Peter said to them, Men, brothers, you know that from days early among you chose the God by the mouth of me to hear the Gentiles the word of the gospel and to believe. \v 8 And the heart-knowing God bore witness to them having given the Spirit the Holy as also to us, \v 9 and not one thing He made distinction between us both and them, by the faith having purified the hearts of them.
pieces: After a long debate, Peter rose and spoke to them: "Brothers, you know that in the early days God made his choice among you: through my mouth the Gentiles were to hear the message of the gospel and come to believe.
God, who knows every heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for us as well.
He made no difference at all between us and them, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cleansed their hearts by faith.

L.7: And after there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them, "Men, brothers, you know that from early days God made a choice among you, that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.
L.8: And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, giving [them] the Holy Spirit just as also to us,
L.9: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made no distinction at all between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.

R.7: The leaders talked about it for a long time. Then Peter stood up and said, "Brothers, you remember what happened some time ago. God chose me from among you to tell the good news to people who are not Jews. He wanted them to hear the message and believe.
R.8: God knows what is in every person's heart. He showed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accepted these Gentiles by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the Spirit to us.
R.9: God did not treat us and them differently. He made their hearts clean because they had faith in Jesus.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: a formal address, here to the apostles and elders
alternatives: an address to the whole church, men and women
decisions.reason: Peter speaks "to them", the apostles and elders who met in 15:6, and they were all men. But 15:12 speaks of the whole crowd and 15:22 of the whole church, so others may have been listening, women among them. The words alone do not settle it.

decisions.choice: from early days God chose: Peter's visit to Cornelius
decisions.reason: Peter means the events of 10:1-48, when Gentiles first heard and believed through him, and he told the Jerusalem church of it in 11:4-18. "Early days" looks back to the first years of the church.

decisions.choice: who knows the heart: God, who sees what a person truly is
decisions.reason: The same title is used in the prayer of 1:24. God looked at their hearts, not at whether they were circumcised (1 Samuel 16:7).

decisions.choice: bore witness: the gift of the Spirit showed that God had accepted them
decisions.reason: In 10:44-47 and 11:15-17 the Spirit came on Cornelius's household as on the apostles at Pentecost, and Peter took this as God's own verdict.

decisions.choice: having cleansed their hearts by faith: faith, not circumcision, made them clean
decisions.reason: In Peter's vision God declared clean what was thought unclean (10:15, 10:28). Here God cleanses the Gentiles' hearts, and does it by faith.

decisions.choice: Brothers, with no setting span
decisions.reason: Following the meaning note, the address is taken as spoken to the apostles and elders, all men, as at 5:35. Literal keeps both Greek words. This is open to review.

decisions.choice: some time ago; showed that he accepted these Gentiles; faith in Jesus
alternatives: from early days; bore witness; faith
decisions.reason: Readable says what Peter's hearers knew: the events of Acts 10, what the gift of the Spirit showed, and in whom they had faith.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word the first time it comes in the speech, and uses "Gentiles" after that.

records.source: νῦν οὖν τί πειράζετε τὸν θεόν, ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν ὃν οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν οὔτε ἡμεῖς ἰσχύσαμεν βαστάσαι;
records.gloss: Now therefore why are you testing the God to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, that neither the fathers of us nor we have been able to bear?
pieces: So why are you now putting God to the test? You would lay on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} nor we ourselves have had the strength to carry.

L.10: Now therefore, why are you testing God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?

R.10: So why are you now testing God? You want to make these followers of Jesus obey the whole law. That is like putting a heavy wooden yoke on their necks. Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could not carry that weight, and neither can we.

decisions.choice: testing God: challenging what God has already shown, as Israel did in the desert
decisions.reason: To test God is to doubt or resist what he has made plain (Exodus 17:2; Deuteronomy 6:16; Acts 5:9). God had shown his will by giving the Spirit (15:8).

decisions.choice: a yoke on the neck: the whole law as a burden laid on them
alternatives: the commandments of God as bad in themselves
decisions.reason: A yoke was the wooden bar laid on the neck of an ox. Jewish teachers spoke of taking up the yoke of the law; Jesus called his own yoke easy (Matthew 11:29-30), and Paul calls the law a yoke of slavery (Galatians 5:1). Peter's point is that no one has kept it in full.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the Gentile believers
decisions.reason: Luke often calls believers "disciples" (6:1, 14:22). Here those who would bear the new yoke are the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: our fathers: our forebears, the generations of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 3:13 and 5:30.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: make these followers of Jesus obey the whole law; heavy wooden yoke
alternatives: put a yoke on the neck of the disciples
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the yoke, as the meaning note does.

records.source: ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ πιστεύομεν σωθῆναι καθ’ ὃν τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι.
records.gloss: But by the grace of [the] Lord Jesus we believe to be saved in [the] same manner [as] they also.
pieces: No, we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, and they are saved in just the same way."

L.11: But we believe [that we are] saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same way as they also [are]."

R.11: No! We believe that the Lord Jesus saves us because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, his kindness that we do not deserve. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves them in exactly the same way."

decisions.choice: through the grace of the Lord Jesus: salvation as his gift, not earned by keeping the law
decisions.reason: "But" sets grace against the yoke of 15:10. The phrase puts Jews and Gentiles on the same footing (Romans 3:22-24; Ephesians 2:8-9).

decisions.choice: we believe that we are saved
alternatives: we believe in order to be saved
decisions.reason: The verb "believe" with an infinitive gives what is believed: that we are saved.

decisions.choice: they: the Gentile believers
decisions.reason: Some have taken "they" as the forebears of verse 10. But the speech is about Jews and Gentiles (15:9), and the surprise is that Jews are saved in the same way as Gentiles, not the other way round.

decisions.choice: grace, his kindness that we do not deserve
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term and explains it.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus saves us because of his grace
alternatives: we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable makes the Lord Jesus the subject, which says the same thing in plainer words.

records.source: Ἐσίγησεν δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, καὶ ἤκουον Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν δι’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Kept silent now all the multitude, and were listening to Barnabas and Paul relating what had done the God signs and wonders among the Gentiles by them.
pieces: The whole gathering grew quiet. Everyone listened to Barnabas and Paul as they told of the signs and wonders God had worked among the Gentiles through them.

L.12: And all the crowd fell silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul as they described what signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

R.12: Everyone there became quiet. They listened while Barnabas and Paul told them about the signs and wonders God had done through them among the Gentiles. These showed God's power.

decisions.choice: the crowd: the whole gathering, the church as well as its leaders
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the whole body of believers in 6:2, 6:5 and 15:30.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: works that point to God and amaze those who see them
decisions.reason: The same pair is used of Jesus (2:22), of the apostles (2:43, 5:12) and of Paul and Barnabas at Iconium (14:3). God did them, "through them".

decisions.choice: Barnabas and Paul: Barnabas named first
decisions.reason: Since 13:13 Luke has mostly named Paul first, but in Jerusalem, where Barnabas was known from the start (4:36-37, 11:22), the order is Barnabas and Paul (also 15:25).

decisions.choice: These showed God's power.
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the signs and wonders showed, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος λέγων· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.
records.gloss: After now the were silent they answered James saying, Men, brothers, hear me.
pieces: When they had finished, James responded, "Brothers, listen to what I have to say.

L.13: And after they fell silent, James answered, saying, "Men, brothers, hear me.

R.13: When they finished speaking, James answered, "Brothers, listen to me.

decisions.choice: James: the brother of the Lord, a leader of the Jerusalem church
decisions.reason: James the son of Zebedee had been killed (12:2). This James is the one Peter sent word to in 12:17, whom Paul calls "the Lord's brother" (Galatians 1:19, 2:9). He leads the church in 21:18.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: a formal address to the apostles and elders
alternatives: an address to the whole church, men and women
decisions.reason: As at 15:7: the meeting is of the apostles and elders, but the whole church may have been listening.

decisions.choice: Brothers, with no setting span
decisions.reason: As at 15:7; Literal keeps both Greek words.

records.source: Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Simeon has related how first the God visited to take out of [the] Gentiles a people for the name of Him.
pieces: Simeon has explained how God first looked with favor on the Gentiles, to take from among them a people to bear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.14: Simeon has related how God first visited [the Gentiles] to take from [the] Gentiles a people for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

R.14: Simon Peter has told us how God first showed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} care for the Gentiles. God chose some of them to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people.

decisions.choice: Simeon: Simon Peter, called by the Hebrew form of his name
decisions.reason: Simeon is the older Hebrew form of Simon, and Peter is called this in 2 Peter 1:1. It suits James, the leader of the Jewish believers in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: visited: came to help, looked on with care
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God coming to his people to save them (Luke 1:68, 1:78, 7:16).

decisions.choice: a people from the Gentiles for his name: Gentiles become God's people too
decisions.reason: "A people" is the word usually used for Israel as God's people. Now God takes such a people from among the Gentiles, to belong to him and bear his name (Deuteronomy 14:2; Zechariah 2:11).

decisions.choice: Simon Peter
decisions.reason: Readable uses the name readers know, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: a people to bear his name; his own people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "for his name" means: belonging to him.

records.source: καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσιν οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται·
records.gloss: And with this agree the words of the prophets, as it is written,
pieces: What the prophets said agrees with this, as it stands written:

L.15: And with this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written,

R.15: This is just what God's prophets said long ago. Scripture says,

decisions.choice: the prophets: the book of the twelve prophets, or the prophets in general
decisions.reason: James quotes Amos, but says "the prophets". The twelve shorter prophets were kept as one book (7:42 calls it "the book of the prophets"), and other prophets also foresaw the nations turning to God (Isaiah 45:20-23; Zechariah 8:20-23).

decisions.choice: this: what Simeon has told, God taking a people from the Gentiles
decisions.reason: "This" picks up 15:14.

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: Readable puts the formula for a quotation in plain words.

records.source: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν, ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφ’ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς, λέγει κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα γνωστὰ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος.
records.gloss: After these things I will return and will rebuild the tabernacle of David which has fallen, and the ruins of it I will rebuild and I will set upright it, \v 17 so that may seek out the remnant of men the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom has been called the name of Me upon them, says [the] Lord doing these things \v 18 known from eternity.
pieces: 'After this I will come back, and I will build again the fallen tent of David. I will build again its ruins and raise it up once more,
so that the rest of humankind may seek the Lord, all the nations that are called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, says the Lord, who does these things,
things made known long ago.'

L.16: 'After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the tent of David which has fallen, and its ruins I will rebuild, and I will set it up again,
L.17: so that the rest of {{gender:people|men}} may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name has been called, says [the] Lord, who does these things,

R.16: 'Later I will come back. David's family is like a tent that has fallen down, but I will build it again. I will rebuild what was ruined and make it stand again.
R.17: Then all other people will look for the Lord. All the nations that I have called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own will look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The Lord says this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do these things.
R.18: He made them known long ago.'

decisions.choice: Amos 9:11-12, quoted in the form of the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: a quotation of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: James's words follow the old Greek translation of Amos, not the Hebrew. In the Hebrew, God rebuilds David's fallen booth so that Israel may possess what is left of Edom and all the nations called by his name. The Greek has "so that the rest of humankind may seek". The Hebrew words for "Edom" and "humankind" are written with almost the same letters, and so are the verbs "possess" and "seek"; the Greek translators read them the second way. Both forms say that the nations will come under the name of Israel's God, which is James's point. The opening words "After these things I will return" stand for Amos's "On that day I will raise up", and may echo Jeremiah 12:15.

decisions.choice: the fallen tent of David: David's royal house and kingdom, brought low
decisions.reason: In Amos the "booth" or "hut" of David is his dynasty, fallen like a shelter in ruins. Its rebuilding is the promise of a king from David's line (2 Samuel 7:11-16). Acts sees the promise kept in Jesus, raised to David's throne (2:30-36, 13:32-37).

decisions.choice: the Lord: in Amos the divine name of Israel's God
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Amos 9:12 the speaker is the Lord, written with the divine name, as is usual in the prophets' "says the LORD". The Greek translation uses the word "Lord" for it.

decisions.choice: on whom my name has been called: who belong to God as his own
alternatives: who call on the name of God
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over you means to be owned by him (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 14:9).

decisions.choice: people: humankind as a whole, not men only
decisions.reason: The rest of humankind are set beside "all the nations".

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "who does these things, known from long ago"
alternatives: many later manuscripts: "who does all these things. Known to God from long ago are all his works"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have the longer wording, which makes a separate sentence. The shorter text, found in early manuscripts, joins the words to the quotation and may echo Isaiah 45:21. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Literal: people, with "men" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable: humankind, all other people
decisions.reason: Following the meaning note. Balanced and Readable use words that are inclusive in themselves.

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek has "Lord", so the English does too, as at 2:34; the meaning note gives the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: David's family is like a tent that has fallen down
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, as the meaning note does.

records.source: διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος·
records.gloss: Therefore I judge not to trouble those who from the Gentiles are turning to the God, \v 20 but to write to them to abstain from the pollutions of the idols and the sexual immorality and the [thing] strangled and the blood.
pieces: So my judgment is that we should not make things hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
Instead we should write to them that they keep away from what idols have defiled, from sexual immorality, from what has been strangled, and from blood.

L.19: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who are turning to God,
L.20: but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols and from sexual immorality and from what is strangled and from blood.

R.19: So I think that we should not make it hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
R.20: Instead, we should write a letter to them. We should tell them not to eat food that has been offered to idols, which makes it unclean. They must not take part in sexual sins. They must not eat meat from animals that were strangled, with the blood still in them. And they must not eat blood.

decisions.choice: I judge: I give my verdict
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to give an opinion or to make a ruling. James speaks as a leader proposing a decision, but the letter says it seemed good to the apostles, the elders and the whole church (15:22, 15:25), so the decision was shared.

decisions.choice: the four things: what the law asked of foreigners living among Israel
decisions.reason: Leviticus 17-18 lays down rules for "the foreigner who lives among you" as well as for Israel: no sacrifices to other gods (17:7-9), no eating of blood (17:10-12), meat from animals properly drained of blood (17:13-14), and no forbidden sexual unions (18:6-26). The four requirements match these closely. Kept by Gentile believers, they made it possible for Jewish and Gentile believers to share life and meals.

decisions.choice: the pollutions of idols: food from sacrifices to idols, defiled by them
decisions.reason: The letter names this as "things sacrificed to idols" (15:29, 21:25). Paul deals with the same question in 1 Corinthians 8-10.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual relations outside marriage, or unions the law forbids
decisions.reason: The word covers every kind of sexual sin. Some take it here to mean the marriages between close relatives forbidden in Leviticus 18, since the other three requirements are about food and the law, but the word is wider than that.

decisions.choice: what is strangled: meat from animals killed without draining the blood
decisions.reason: An animal strangled or caught in a snare still had its blood in it, which the law forbade (Leviticus 17:13-14; Deuteronomy 12:16, 12:23).

decisions.choice: blood: eating or drinking blood
decisions.reason: The law forbade eating blood, because the life is in the blood (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:11). In the Western form of the text, which drops "what is strangled" (see the next note), "blood" can be read as murder.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: four requirements, with "what is strangled"
alternatives: Codex Bezae and other Western witnesses: no "what is strangled", and the added words "and not to do to others what they would not want done to themselves"
decisions.reason: In the Western text, mainly Codex Bezae, the list is three: idols, sexual immorality and blood. Without "strangled" the list can be read as rules of conduct (idolatry, sexual sin, murder), and the added saying, a form of the Golden Rule put negatively, fits that reading. The same changes are found in 15:29. The four-part list stands in the other manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not to eat food offered to idols; meat from animals that were strangled, with the blood still in them
alternatives: to abstain from the pollutions of idols ... what is strangled and blood
decisions.reason: Readable says what each requirement meant, as the meaning notes explain.

decisions.choice: I think
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word; the meaning note explains its weight.

L.21: For Moses from ancient generations has in every city those who proclaim him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath."

R.21: For a very long time the law of Moses has been taught in every city. Every Sabbath day people read it aloud in the synagogues."

decisions.reason: "For" gives a reason, but James does not say how it connects. Most likely: Jews who know the law live in every city, so Gentile believers should respect these points for their sake. Another reading is that the law already has its teachers, and the Gentiles need not be made to keep it all.

decisions.choice: Moses: the law given through Moses, the books of Moses
decisions.reason: As in Luke 16:29 and 24:27, "Moses" stands for the writings of the law.

decisions.choice: read in the synagogues every Sabbath: the regular reading of the law

decisions.choice: Moses has been preached; the law of Moses has been taught

records.gloss: Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders with all the church, having chosen men out from them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas, Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, men leading among the brothers, \v 23 having written by [the] hand of them, The apostles and the elders brothers To those in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia brothers those from among [the] Gentiles Greetings.
pieces: Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, decided to pick men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, known as Barsabbas, and Silas, men who held leading places among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
They sent with them this letter: "From the apostles and the elders, your brothers, to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} of Gentile birth in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: greetings.

L.22: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send [them] to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}},
L.23: having written by their hand: "The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} from among [the] Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, greetings.

R.22: Then the apostles and the elders and the whole church decided to choose some men from their group. They would send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, who was also called Barsabbas, and Silas. These two men were leaders among the believers.
R.23: They gave them a letter to take with them. It said: "We, the apostles and the elders, are your brothers. We are writing to you, our fellow believers who are not Jews, in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia. We send you our greetings.

decisions.choice: it seemed good: they decided, as a formal resolution
decisions.reason: This is the language of official decisions, and it is repeated in the letter (15:25, 15:28).

decisions.choice: Judas Barsabbas and Silas: leaders of the Jerusalem church
decisions.reason: Silas becomes Paul's companion from 15:40, and is likely the Silvanus of Paul's letters (2 Corinthians 1:19; 1 Thessalonians 1:1; 1 Peter 5:12). Judas Barsabbas may be a relative of the Joseph Barsabbas of 1:23, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: brothers: the apostles and elders call themselves brothers of those they write to
alternatives: a third group of senders, the brothers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" stands beside "the apostles and the elders" and describes them. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "and the brothers", making the whole church senders as well. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Antioch, Syria and Cilicia: the city, and the Roman province around it
decisions.reason: Antioch was the chief city of Syria; Syria and Cilicia were governed together at this time. Paul had worked in this area (Galatians 1:21; Acts 9:30, 11:25-26).

decisions.choice: having written by their hand ... greetings: the letter carried by them, in the usual form of a Greek letter
decisions.reason: "By their hand" means the letter was sent with them. "Greetings" is how Greek letters began (23:26; James 1:1).

decisions.choice: From ... your brothers
alternatives: The apostles and the elders, brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the opening of the letter in the form English letters use.

decisions.choice: We, the apostles and the elders, are your brothers. We are writing to you ... We send you our greetings.
alternatives: The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the brothers ... greetings
decisions.reason: Readable turns the greeting formula into full sentences.

decisions.choice: brothers, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The senders are the apostles and elders, men, so the word is not widened. The readers, "the brothers from among the Gentiles", are believers, men and women, and take the setting.

So we have come to one mind and decided to choose men and send them to you with Barnabas and Paul, whom we love,

L.24: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your minds, to whom we gave no instructions,
L.25: it seemed good to us, having come to one mind, to choose men and send [them] to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
L.26: men who have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: unsettling: turning upside down, throwing into confusion
decisions.reason: The verb was used of tearing down or packing up a house and moving out. It pictures their minds thrown into disorder.

decisions.choice: to whom we gave no instructions: the Jerusalem church did not send them
alternatives: sent them, but with other instructions
decisions.reason: The letter distances the church from the teachers of 15:1.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence goes on without saying what they taught
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "saying, You must be circumcised and keep the law"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add these words, which repeat 15:1 and 15:5. Early manuscripts do not have them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: handed over their lives: risked their lives, or gave their lives up to serve
decisions.reason: The words can mean to put one's life at risk, as Paul had at Lystra (14:19), or to give one's life over to a cause. Both fit, and both say that they had held nothing back for the Lord's name.

decisions.choice: for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: for his sake, for his cause
decisions.reason: As in 5:41 and 9:16, the name stands for the person.

decisions.choice: some people from our church; We did not send them
alternatives: some who went out from us; to whom we gave no instructions
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the church did not send the teachers, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: have put their lives in danger to serve our Lord
alternatives: have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord
decisions.reason: Readable takes the first sense in the meaning note and explains the idiom of the name.

decisions.choice: whom we love; our dear friends
decisions.reason: "Beloved" is a church word; Balanced and Readable use plain English.

decisions.choice: we have sent: written from the readers' point of view

decisions.choice: the same things: what the letter says

decisions.choice: we are sending

decisions.choice: what we have written in this letter
decisions.reason: Readable names what "the same things" are.

pieces: The Holy Spirit and we ourselves have decided to place on you no burden beyond these essentials:
keep away from food offered to idols, from blood, from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you guard yourselves against these, you will be doing what is right.

L.28: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay on you no greater burden than these necessary things:
L.29: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well.

R.29: Do not eat food that has been offered to idols. Do not eat blood, or meat from animals that were strangled. And do not take part in sexual sins. If you stay away from these things, you will be doing what is right.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit and us: the decision is the Spirit's leading, which the church agreed with
alternatives: a human decision with a pious phrase
decisions.reason: The Spirit's guidance had been seen in the gift of the Spirit to the Gentiles (15:8) and in the Scriptures (15:15-18). The leaders claim no authority of their own apart from it (5:32, 13:2).

decisions.choice: burden: a load, here the obligations of the law
decisions.reason: The word picks up Peter's yoke of 15:10. The four requirements are all that is asked.

decisions.choice: things sacrificed to idols: meat from animals offered in pagan sacrifice
decisions.reason: The letter names plainly what James called "the pollutions of idols" (15:20). Such meat was eaten at temple feasts and sold in the market (1 Corinthians 8:1-13, 10:25-28).

decisions.choice: the order of the list: idols, blood, what is strangled, sexual immorality
decisions.reason: The letter gives the same four requirements as James did in 15:20, but puts the three about food together. Acts 21:25 has the same order.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: four requirements, with "what is strangled"
alternatives: Codex Bezae and other Western witnesses: no "what is strangled", and the added negative Golden Rule
decisions.reason: As in 15:20, the Western text drops "what is strangled" and adds a saying about not doing to others what you would not want done to yourself. Codex Bezae also adds "being carried along by the Holy Spirit" after "you will do well". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you will do well: you will be doing what is right
decisions.reason: The phrase was a common polite close in letters and can mean either "you will act rightly" or "things will go well for you". After a list of requirements, the first fits better.

decisions.choice: The Holy Spirit has shown us what to do, and we agree.
alternatives: it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us
decisions.reason: Readable explains how the Spirit and the church decided together, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: Do not eat food ...; do not eat blood, or meat from animals that were strangled
alternatives: abstain from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled
decisions.reason: As at 15:20, Readable says what each requirement meant.

alternatives: they; those who had sent them
decisions.reason: Readable names the people and the place, from 15:22-27.

records.source: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: Paul however and Barnabas stayed in Antioch teaching and proclaiming the good news with also others many the word of the Lord.
pieces: Paul and Barnabas, though, stayed on in Antioch. Along with many others, they taught the word of the Lord and proclaimed it as good news.

L.35: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming as good news, with many others also, the word of the Lord.

R.35: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. They and many other believers taught people the message about the Lord Jesus and told them the good news.

decisions.choice: the word of the Lord: the message about the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 8:25 and 13:44-49, the message the apostles preached.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the good news: announcing the gospel
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the noun for gospel (15:7).

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord, following the meaning note.

records.source: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρναβᾶν Παῦλος· Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πόλιν πᾶσαν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.
records.gloss: After now some days said to Barnabas Paul, Having turned back indeed let us look after the brothers in city every in which we have announced the word of the Lord, how they are.
pieces: Some days later Paul said to Barnabas, "Come, let us go back and look in on the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every town where we announced the word of the Lord, and find out how they are doing."

L.36: And after some days Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back now and visit the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, [to see] how they are."

R.36: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, "We should go back and visit the believers in all the towns where we told people the message about the Lord. Let us see how they are doing."

decisions.choice: visit: go to see and care for
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of God visiting in 15:14: looking after people with concern.

decisions.choice: every city where we proclaimed: the towns of the first journey
alternatives: all the cities of the empire
decisions.reason: Paul means Cyprus and the towns of southern Galatia: Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe (13:4-14:25).

decisions.choice: now: a word that gives urgency
decisions.reason: The small word adds force to the suggestion: come now, let us go.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: As at 15:1.

records.heading: Paul and Barnabas go separate ways

records.source: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μᾶρκον·
records.gloss: Barnabas now purposed to take along also John the [one] called Mark.
pieces: Barnabas wanted to bring John, also called Mark, with them too.

L.37: And Barnabas wanted to take along also John, who was called Mark.

R.37: Barnabas wanted to take John Mark with them again.

decisions.choice: John called Mark: Barnabas's cousin, who had begun the first journey with them
decisions.reason: His mother's house was a meeting place of the Jerusalem church (12:12). He came to Antioch with Barnabas and Saul (12:25) and set out with them as a helper (13:5). Colossians 4:10 calls him Barnabas's cousin.

decisions.choice: wanted: kept wanting, insisted
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense suggests a settled wish that Barnabas held to, set against Paul's view in 15:38.

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Readable says that Mark had gone with them before, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.
records.gloss: Paul however thought fit the [one] having withdrawn from them from Pamphylia and not having gone with them to the work not to take along this [one].
pieces: But Paul did not think it right to take with them a man who had left them in Pamphylia and had not gone on with them to the work.

L.38: But Paul thought it not right to take along this one, who had withdrawn from them from Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.

R.38: But Paul did not think they should take him. On their first trip Mark had left them in Pamphylia. He did not stay with them to finish the work.

decisions.choice: withdrew from them from Pamphylia: Mark's return to Jerusalem in 13:13
decisions.reason: At Perga in Pamphylia John left them and went back to Jerusalem (13:13). Luke does not give his reasons.

decisions.choice: withdrawn: gone away, left
decisions.reason: The verb means to go away or to fall away. In Paul's eyes Mark's leaving was a failure to stand by the work, but the word does not by itself say that he betrayed them.

decisions.choice: the work: the mission God had called them to
decisions.reason: The work for which the Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul apart (13:2, 14:26).

decisions.choice: on their first trip
decisions.reason: Readable says when this happened.

records.source: ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμὸς ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρναβᾶν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μᾶρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον, Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ τὴν Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.
records.gloss: Arose therefore a sharp disagreement, so that separated they from one another, and Barnabas having taken Mark sailed to Cyprus. \v 40 Paul however having chosen Silas went forth, having been committed to the grace of the Lord by the brothers. \v 41 He was passing through then Syria and Cilicia strengthening the churches.
pieces: The quarrel grew so heated that the two of them parted ways. Barnabas took Mark and sailed off to Cyprus,
while Paul picked Silas and set out, after the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} had commended him to the grace of the Lord.
He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches strong.

L.39: And there was a sharp disagreement, so that they separated from one another, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus.
L.40: But Paul chose Silas and went out, having been entrusted to the grace of the Lord by the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
L.41: And he was going through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

R.39: Paul and Barnabas disagreed so strongly that they split up. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed to the island of Cyprus.
R.40: Paul chose Silas to go with him. The believers prayed that the Lord would bless them with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, and then Paul and Silas left.
R.41: They went through Syria and Cilicia and helped the churches there grow strong in their faith.

decisions.choice: a sharp disagreement: a heated clash, with strong feeling on both sides
decisions.reason: The word is used of being stirred up or provoked (17:16; 1 Corinthians 13:5). Luke tells of the quarrel plainly and does not say who was right. Later Paul speaks well of both men (1 Corinthians 9:6; Colossians 4:10; 2 Timothy 4:11).

decisions.choice: Cyprus: Barnabas's home island, where the first journey began
decisions.reason: Barnabas came from Cyprus (4:36), and it was their first stop in 13:4.

decisions.choice: entrusted to the grace of the Lord: sent off with prayer for the Lord's help
decisions.reason: As in 14:26, the church committed the missionaries to the Lord's care and favor for the work ahead.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "of the Lord"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "of God", as in 14:26. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he was going through: Paul, with Silas
decisions.reason: The verb is singular because Paul leads, but Silas is with him (16:1-3 names them both).

decisions.choice: the churches of Syria and Cilicia: the churches the letter was written to
decisions.reason: These are the churches addressed in 15:23, so Paul and Silas bring them the decision (16:4).

decisions.choice: The believers prayed that the Lord would bless them with his grace
alternatives: having been entrusted to the grace of the Lord by the brothers
decisions.reason: Readable says what entrusting to grace meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: They went; helped the churches there grow strong in their faith
decisions.reason: Readable names both travelers and says in what way the churches were strengthened.
